hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: Traverse both sorted time series simultaneously in chronological order.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: When timestamps match, combine their values into a single consolidated record.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Otherwise append the entry bearing the earlier timestamp and advance its pointer.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def aggregateTimeSeries(series1: list[list[int]], series2: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
    i = 0
    j = 0
    m, n = len(series1), len(series2)
    res = []
    while i < m and j < n:
        t1, v1 = series1[i]
        t2, v2 = series2[j]
        if t1 == t2:
            res.append([t1, v1 + v2])
            i += 1
            j += 1
        elif t1 < t2:
            res.append([t1, v1])
            i += 1
        else:
            res.append([t2, v2])
            j += 1
    while i < m:
        res.append(series1[i])
        i += 1
    while j < n:
        res.append(series2[j])
        j += 1
    return res
```

complexity.notes: Two pointer linear merge of sorted chronological time series.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Concatenating and re-sorting timestamps adds an unnecessary O(N log N) overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Merged series output stores combined timestamp records.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applies standard merge step of two sorted lists.
